action.action-desc: Mr. Latta introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce

form.official-title: To amend title I of the Communications Act of 1934 to provide for internet openness, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Open Internet Act of 2019.
Title I of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 151 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following new section:

subsection.header: Duties of broadband internet access service providers

paragraph.text: To the extent that a person is engaged in the provision of broadband internet access service, such person—

subparagraph.text: shall not block lawful content, applications, or services, or prohibit the use of non-harmful devices, subject to reasonable network management;
shall not unjustly or unreasonably discriminate in transmitting lawful traffic over a consumer’s broadband internet access service; and
shall disclose accurate and relevant information in plain language regarding the price, performance, and network management practices of such person’s broadband internet access service sufficient—

clause.text: for consumers to make informed choices regarding use of such service; and
for content, application, service, and device providers to develop and market new internet offerings.

paragraph.text: The Commission may promulgate rules to implement paragraph (1)(C). Any such rules—

subparagraph.text: shall require, at a minimum, such person to display or provide links to the required information on an internet website and to update such information in a timely fashion to reflect material changes in the information subject to such paragraph; and
shall not require public disclosure of—

clause.text: information that would compromise network security; or
information that would undermine the efficacy of reasonable network management practices.

paragraph.text: For purposes of paragraph (1)(B), reasonable network management shall not be construed to be unjustly or unreasonably discriminatory.

The Commission shall enforce the duties established in subsections (a)(1)(A) and (a)(1)(B) through adjudication of a complaint alleging that a service violates one or more of such duties. Nothing in this section limits the Commission’s authority to adopt procedures for the adjudication of a complaint, to adopt an order requiring compliance from an entity subject to a complaint, to initiate an enforcement action, or to issue a declaratory ruling or guidance.

If the Commission finds that a provider of broadband internet access service has violated any provision of subsection (a), the Commission may issue an order enjoining such violation, including interim injunctive relief. If the Commission finds that a provider of broadband internet access service has engaged in a willful and knowing violation of such subsection, the Commission may issue a fine or forfeiture of no more than $2,000,000 for any practice found to violate such subsection, consistent with the procedures in section 503. The Commission may not order the payment of damages for any violation of such subsection.
Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize any private right of action in court.

subsection.header: Relationship to other titles and laws

paragraph.text: The Commission may not impose regulations on broadband internet access service or any component thereof under title II, except in the event that a provider of broadband internet access service elects to provide the transmission component of such service as a telecommunications service under such title. Except as expressly provided in this section, nothing in this section shall increase, reduce, or otherwise alter the Commission’s authority.

Nothing in this section shall supersede any obligation or authorization a provider of broadband internet access service may have, or limit the provider’s ability, to address the needs of emergency communications, law enforcement, public safety, or national security, consistent with applicable law. Nothing in this section shall prohibit reasonable efforts by a provider of broadband internet access service to address copyright infringement or other unlawful activity.
Nothing in this section shall increase, reduce, or otherwise alter the antitrust or other authorities of the Department of Justice or the Federal Trade Commission.

subparagraph.text: The term broadband internet access service means a mass-market retail service by wire or radio that provides the capability to transmit data to and receive data from all or substantially all internet endpoints, including any capabilities that are incidental to and enable the operation of the communications service, but excluding dial-up internet access service.
The term includes any service that—

clause.text: the Commission finds to be providing a functional equivalent of the service described in subparagraph (A); or
is used to evade the protections set forth in this section.

subparagraph.text: The term reasonable network management means a network management practice that is appropriate and tailored to achieving a legitimate network management function, taking into account the particular network architecture or technology of the provider.
The term includes appropriate and tailored practices—

clause.text: to reduce or mitigate the effects of congestion on a broadband internet access service provider’s network;
to ensure network security or integrity;
to address traffic that is harmful to or unwanted by—
to meet the needs of public safety; and
to provide services or capabilities consistent with a consumer’s choices regarding parental control or security capabilities.

subparagraph.text: In determining whether a network management practice is reasonable, the Commission shall consider technical requirements, standards, or best practices adopted by one or more independent, widely recognized internet community governance initiatives or standard-setting organizations.
